title: A Credit Card Paid Delta More Than Its Profit ✈️ #shorts
description:
In 2025, American Express paid Delta Air Lines $8.2 billion for SkyMiles, while Delta's adjusted pre-tax profit for the whole year was about $5 billion. Airlines don't just sell seats, they sell points.
Source: Delta Air Lines December quarter & full year 2025 results (Jan 13, 2026); Fortune, "Delta sees wealthy high fliers..." (Jan 13, 2026). Education, not financial advice.
script: A credit card paid Delta Air Lines more money last year than the airline made in profit.
In twenty twenty-five, American Express paid Delta eight point two billion dollars.
Delta's entire pre-tax profit that year? About five billion.
So why would a card company pay an airline?
Because Delta sells its SkyMiles to American Express.
Amex hands those miles to you every time you swipe, and the store pays a small fee on every purchase.
Miles are cheap for Delta to create. Flying planes is not.
The airline isn't just selling seats. It's selling points.
